per_window.ps-ns: Reference state (reduced Cu(I), pH 5.5, 41 °C, the RelaxDB sample, full text of doi:10.1021/bi990624l): dynamic_in_window at the loop 103-108, the turn 74-77 (K74 S2 0.69, tau_e 1.3 ns; D77 0.70), I7 and the C-terminal L127-K128 (J37, D-r1); the rest of the backbone, including the copper ligands H46 and H117 (S2 0.97) and the loop 112-121, is rigid with average S2 0.86 ± 0.05 (J41, no_evidence_in_window), and the W48 indole has S2 0.89 (J42, D-r2). Oxidised Cu(II): no per-residue order parameters in any row (J1, search_insufficient). Reduced Cu(I) at other conditions: an abstract calls H117 and the hydrophobic patch mobile and N47-V49 relatively rigid (J17, r16, r17). The homologous CuA domain is rigid on this scale in apo and holo forms (r47, r48, not judged).
per_window.us-ms: Reference state (reduced Cu(I), pH 5.5, 41 °C, 600 MHz): dynamic_in_window around His35: N10, D11, G37, G45 (9.5 Hz), G88, S89, G90 carry Rex of 2-9.5 Hz that the authors reproduce with the His35 protonation equilibrium (deprotonated form 2-4%, k = 60 ± 30 s-1, lifetime 8 ± 4 ms, slow on the chemical-shift timescale; 15N shift differences 340-400 Hz), plus F114 in the copper loop without a mechanism and weak Rex about 1 Hz in the flap 53-79 (J43, D-r3). Reduced Cu(I) at pH about 5, 50 mM phosphate (2003 CPMG at three fields): two processes, one around H35 (D11, G37, G88-G90; kA 11.7 ± 2.4 s-1, 0.39 ± 0.07% at 44.8 °C; J12, r9) and one in the copper loops (N47, W48, F111-T113, G116, H117, L120, K122; kA 4.1 ± 0.1 s-1, 0.45 ± 0.02%; J13, r10); residues in between sense both (J14, r11); per-residue kA 0.44-9.55 s-1 at 35.4 °C (J15, r12); 29 named amides pass across 25.7-44.8 °C (J16, r13-r15). Copper-free apo at 298 K, pH 7.0 (another sample state since 2026-10-20): 17 amides around the metal site broadened out by intermediate exchange (J18, r44), dispersion at M44, I87 and two more regions (J19, r45), none at T61 (J20, r46); high-pH 1H broadening of histidines, abstract only (J22). Oxidised Cu(II): not measured (J2). Homolog apo CuA shows the same pattern (J36).
per_window.slower_than_ms: Reduced Cu(I) at pH 7.0, 41 °C (full text of the RelaxDB source paper): dynamic_in_window; two resolved peak sets for the nuclei around His35 interconvert with k = 45 ± 6 s-1 (kex 90 s-1, lifetime 11 ± 2 ms, equal populations at the pKa 7.0 ± 0.1) by EXSY, which the authors read as the slow His35 protonation/deprotonation equilibrium that interconverts the pH 5.5 and pH 9.0 crystal conformations in solution; computed kex/delta-omega about 0.04, slow exchange (J38, D-r4, D-r5). The same process at pH 5.5 is carried by J43 in the us-ms window because it is seen there as exchange broadening with a model-derived lifetime of 8 ± 4 ms. Oxidised Cu(II): not measured as such (J3). The Cu(I) forward rates of 4-12 s-1 from the 2003 CPMG fits stay in the us-ms window. Single-molecule ET-rate fluctuations over tens to hundreds of seconds (J33) are electron-transfer kinetics, not conformational.
per_window.undetermined: Static and indirect items, none counted as exchange: oxidised crystals at two pH values with a P36-G37 flip (J4, abstract; the RelaxDB source paper's own comparison of these crystals with its solution exchange pattern is J44, D-r6, structure_only); DEPC histidine accessibility (J5); femtosecond coherences and charge transfer (J6, photophysics); holo fluorescence heterogeneity (J7, abstract); forced unfolding by steered MD and AFM (J8, J9, J26, J27); ionic-liquid and electrode studies (J10, J11); two apo crystal forms (J21, abstract); W48 phosphorescence and acrylamide quenching in apo and Cd forms (J23, J24, J29); 3 μs MD of apo and Zn azurin with loop fluctuation and water entry (J25, J30, md_only); Fe-, Zn-, Co- and Ni-substituted crystals (J28, J31, J32, J40); temperature-jump slow phase of the azurin/cytochrome c551 mixture assigned to H35 (J39, C-r3, abstract); Ru- and Re-labelled constructs (J34, J35, ET and photophysics). Not judged (mutants, engineered loops or metal sites, static crystals, chemical or ET assays): phosphorescence of I7S, F110S, C3A/C26A, F110A, F29A and Y108A (r3-r8, r22-r25, r28-r43); fluorescence anisotropy of I7S and F110S (r18, r19); C112A and C26A polyproteins and reduced-disulfide MD (r55, r56, r58); C3S and C3S/S100P folding (r68, r69); type-zero C112D/M121L EXAFS (r86); M121A Fe-azide ligand exchange (r89, binding kinetics); CuA homolog relaxation (r47, r48); p28 peptide and docking MD (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r3, r5, r6); W48/W108 hydration MD (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r4); Y72F/Y108F radical decay (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r9); H46E/M121H iron nitrosyl (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r10, r11); H117A/M121H crystals (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r12, r13); GPLGS and junction MD abstracts (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r14, r15); N47D/S/L KC-RPMD (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r17-r19); DEPC mutants (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r31-r33); I7S and F110S crystals (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-r38, r39); and all AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020005254-rows (M121A, T21R1 spin label, redox-tuning, nitrotyrosine, M121E, loop-shortened, C112D/M121X, Ru crystal, thermostability, W48M, F114A, H117G, N47D, H20/Y48, crosslinked dimers, CuA and loop-length chimeras), including the abstract-only multitemperature B-factor study whose construct is unresolved (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020005254-r22). Also not judged, from the 2026-10-20 re-read (C-rN): N42C disulfide dimer electron self-exchange (C-r4, ET kinetics); oxidised apo-H117G and apo-H46G crystals (C-r6, r7, mutants); M44K EPR/ESEEM (C-r9, mutant, not DEER); classical and QM/MM excited-state MD of the Re124W and Re126WW photosensitiser constructs, including a 6% trajectory occupancy of a dmp-away orientation and sub-picosecond solvent response (C-r10 to r13, engineered constructs, chromophore motion).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes for the RelaxDB sample, which is reduced Cu(I) azurin (2 mM, 20 mM potassium phosphate, pH 5.5, 41 °C, 600 MHz; reference state since 2026-10-20, copper-bound, not copper-free): the amides of N10, D11, G37, G45, G88, S89 and G90 around His35 show exchange broadening of 2-9.5 Hz that the authors explain by the His35 protonation/deprotonation equilibrium, slow on the chemical-shift timescale, with a deprotonated minor form of 2-4% at pH 5.5, k = 60 ± 30 s-1 (lifetime 8 ± 4 ms) and 15N shift differences of 340-400 Hz; at pH 7.0 the two forms give two resolved peak sets with EXSY cross-peaks and k = 45 ± 6 s-1 (lifetime 11 ± 2 ms, equal populations) (J43, J38; full text of doi:10.1021/bi990624l). The exchange is protonation-coupled, so whether it counts as an alternate conformational state is a question for the NMR collaborator. Copper-free apo azurin (298 K, pH 7.0, 100 mM phosphate, 2 mM DTT) is a different sample state with 17 amides lost to intermediate exchange and CPMG dispersion at M44 and I87, no rate or population (J18, J19); oxidised Cu(II) azurin has no exchange measurement.
open_conflicts: Not a conflict but a state contrast: apo-azurin loses 17 amides to intermediate exchange, while the authors cite a full Cu(I) HSQC (all non-proline residues but A1); the apo (pH 7.0, 100 mM phosphate, DTT) and Cu(I) (pH about 5, 50 mM phosphate) samples also differ in pH and buffer, so metal state and pH are confounded.
Residue 116: the CPMG paper's Table 2 prints 'Cys 116' while the entry sequence has G116; the judgments follow the sequence (row AZURIN-r10 still prints C116).

H35 process rate in reduced Cu(I) azurin: the 1999 RelaxDB source paper gives k = 60 ± 30 s-1 at pH 5.5 (kex about 120 s-1, minor form 2-4% estimated from the pKa; J43) and k = 45 ± 6 s-1 at pH 7.0 by EXSY (J38), whereas the 2003 three-field CPMG fit at pH about 5, 44.8 °C gives kA 11.7 ± 2.4 s-1 with a 0.39% minor state and keq 254, i.e. kex in the thousands per second (r9, J12); the two papers use different models (equal-population line broadening with a pKa-derived correction versus Carver-Richards with a fitted minor population), different phosphate concentrations and slightly different pH, so the rates are not reconciled.
Within the 1999 paper the mean S2 is 0.85 ± 0.05 in the abstract and 0.86 ± 0.05 in the Results; both are kept.
questions_for_gina: The RelaxDB AZURIN sample is reduced Cu(I) azurin at pH 5.5 and 41 °C (doi:10.1021/bi990624l, full text). Its slow exchange around His35 is a protonation/deprotonation equilibrium (deprotonated form 2-4% at pH 5.5, two resolved peak sets near pH 7) that interconverts the pH 5.5 and pH 9.0 crystal conformations: should a pH-coupled chemical equilibrium of a metal-bound sample count as an alternate APO state in the 2026-09-17 sense?

The 1999 line-broadening rate (k = 60 ± 30 s-1, pH 5.5) and EXSY rate (45 ± 6 s-1, pH 7.0) disagree with the 2003 three-field CPMG model of the same Cu(I) H35 process (kA 11.7 s-1, pB 0.39%, kex in the thousands per second); which model should the atlas carry for the reference state?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Every NMR dynamics sample is in phosphate: 20 mM, pH 5.5 (RelaxDB sample, D-r1 to r3) or pH 7.0 (D-r4, r5) for the 1999 reduced Cu(I) study, 50 mM, pH about 5 for the 2003 Cu(I) CPMG (r9-r15) and 100 mM, pH 7.0 with 2 mM DTT for apo (r44-r46); no row tests a phosphate effect or a buffer change. The apo protein was made by KCN dialysis. Phosphorescence work (r1-r43) uses 2 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 at 20 °C with Cd(II) or Zn(II) standing in for copper. Reference state since 2026-10-20: the RelaxDB sample is reduced Cu(I) azurin (dithionite under argon), 2 mM, 20 mM potassium phosphate, pH 5.5, 41 °C, 600 MHz, 90% H2O/10% D2O (D-r1), so is_wt_apo marks the Cu(I) pH 5.5 judgments (J37, J41-J43) and the copper-free apo judgments (J18-J26) are another sample state. The 1999 relaxation analysis used one field, a fixed 1 ms CPMG spacing and isotropic tumbling; the pH 7.0 EXSY sample is nonlabelled and its Cu(I) state is inferred from the general preparation. Row-id shorthand: A-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-rN, B-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020005254-rN, C-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020143153-rN (abstract-only reads of the 1999 paper, superseded by the full-text D rows on 2026-10-20 and no longer cited), D-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020202618-rN. Second reads of the D rows: r1 corrected (pooled residue list replaced by the authors' flexible set), r4 and r5 reclassified as 'other', r3 identities N10, D11, S89 confirmed from the mature sequence (ledger/adjudication_AZURIN_pdf.json).
